note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: MARS-RA: motivation, method, theory, and empirical results

nodes.name: Embodied credit assignment is hard
nodes.description: Embodied multi-agent credit assignment is exacerbated by partial noisy egocentric multimodal observations with sparse, delayed rewards, and by open systems where agents enter or leave mid-task, violating fixed-agent-set assumptions.

nodes.name: Existing methods degrade
nodes.description: Credit assignment methods like QMIX and COMA already degrade under insufficient feedback, and prior LLM-based credit assignment relies on simplified environments, handcrafted rules and strong assumptions.

nodes.name: Credit as rank aggregation
nodes.description: MARS-RA reformulates credit assignment as rank aggregation: each agent's credit is a latent contribution score inferred from pairwise comparisons of which agent contributes more, replacing absolute with relative estimation.

nodes.name: LMM pairwise comparisons
nodes.description: An LMM, prompted as a referee with task context, agent-image mapping, comparative reasoning and JSON output, compares egocentric observations of active-agent pairs in both orders (to mitigate position bias), skipping when fewer than 2 agents are active.

nodes.name: Bradley-Terry aggregation
nodes.description: The comparison matrix is aggregated with a Bradley-Terry model by MLE into per-agent contribution scores, which handles noise and yields cardinal values for smooth rewards.

nodes.name: Potential-based shaping
nodes.description: Scores are softmax-normalized into a potential (zero at terminal states) and used for potential-based reward shaping with weight rho, preserving policy invariance while the scores evolve during training.

nodes.name: Convergence and robustness bound
nodes.description: If the comparison graph is connected, with probability at least 1-n^-2 the MLE error to the latent preference is bounded by C0*sqrt(n log n / K)/sqrt(n) with K comparisons, so more comparisons filter out LMM noise.

nodes.name: Shapley interpretation
nodes.description: If the LMM's latent preference equals true Shapley values, MARS-RA scores are consistent estimators of them up to a translation constant, an idealized interpretive lens rather than a practical claim.

nodes.name: MARS-Bench
nodes.description: MARS-Bench in ManiSkill3 has three tasks (Pass Gate, Herd Sheep, Collect Ball) with 2-4 agents, egocentric pixel observations, sparse rewards, and battery depletion that removes and later respawns agents, creating open agent counts.

nodes.name: MARS-RA outperforms baselines
nodes.description: All baselines (MAPPO, QMIX, COMA, SQDDPG, SAMA, V-GEPF) stay below 50% success on MARS-Bench while MARS-RA keeps success above 47% on all three tasks and exceeds 70% on Herd Sheep.

nodes.name: LMM comparisons are consistent
nodes.description: LMM pairwise judgments are consistent, with a 3-cycle rate of 8.95% versus 25.00% for random and held-out 3-way NLL of 0.41 versus 1.10 for random.

nodes.name: Rank aggregation beats direct scoring
nodes.description: The LMM Score variant, which has the LMM directly output contribution scores, shows oscillation and weaker performance than rank aggregation, even though LMM spatio-temporal inference helps.

nodes.name: Better LMMs and more queries help
nodes.description: Performance rises with LMM comparison accuracy (Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-5.1 above 70%; Qwen3-VL 2B/4B/8B above 43%) and number of queries, with gains from more queries larger for lower-accuracy LMMs.

nodes.name: Generalizes to standard MARL
nodes.description: MARS-RA is comparable to SAMA on five Overcooked tasks and remains effective on 10-agent Pistonball, suggesting benefit beyond small teams and MARS-Bench.

isolated_nodes.name: Rank Centrality is slightly worse
isolated_nodes.description: Using Rank Centrality instead of Bradley-Terry yields slightly lower success on MARS-Bench, with a small gap (Table 1).

isolated_nodes.name: Errors when views lack cues
isolated_nodes.description: Pairwise comparison errors occur most often when all agents face a wall with no informative visual cues; they stay accurate if at least one agent's observation is informative.

isolated_nodes.name: No benchmark supports dynamic agents
isolated_nodes.description: Existing multi-agent embodied benchmarks such as MQE and TDW-Cook do not support a dynamic number of active agents.

structural_reasoning: Embodied-setting challenges motivate rank aggregation; the pipeline from LMM comparison to BT scores to shaping underlies theory and the benchmark results.
